_what: THE JUDGE'S OWN SELF-TEST — a deck whose BUILD SLOT holds a frame Rafe personally culled.
.claude/skills/frame-critic/run_frame_critic.sh \
--config .claude/skills/frame-critic/evidence/selftest-floor.json \
--build-frame .claude/skills/frame-critic/morgue/keyline-floor.png
The declared expectation is that the seat flags it. If a seat would ship a culled frame, the
mechanism has told us its own judging layer is soft — which is the one thing it exists to be
able to say.
WHY THE FLOOR SURFACE AND NOT THE WALL. `--build-frame` excludes its own file from the plant
draw, because a deck showing the seat the same picture twice would be the control judging
itself. The wall lane holds ONE morgue entry, so excluding it leaves nothing to draw. The
floor lane holds three, so the self-test runs there — and the picture in the build slot is
still a real culled frame, which is all the test needs.
No capture command runs: --build-frame supplies the frame. The block below is present so the
config is well formed and so the path is obvious if someone points this file at a live round.
The Yarl crop is the wall config's engine-reported viewport band. Same renderer, same
750x1334 capture, same HUD, so the same band — the floor logs of this vintage predate the
grid-map line that reports it, which is why it is inherited rather than read.
The bar crop is the CORRECTED one — twice corrected. The box inherited from
tools/tier1_floors/run_seats.py ran 24 rows off a 720x504 source and PIL padded the
difference with black; shifting it up then ran into the example sheet's own white paper
margin. The artwork occupies x 24-695, y 24-479. See the note in docs/FRAME-CRITIC.json.
_approved_capture_note: NULL, and docs/GATE-CONDITIONS.json explains why for the floor at length: no floor capture
was ever approved outright — the verdicts run 'not wowed, impressed, close', 'closer,
legitimately impressed, one axis remains', 'passed in kind', and a run of FAILs. Naming one
myself would be choosing the baseline my own work is judged against.
